key_insight: NEOPIC learns plasma field operators directly from particle distributions, avoiding meshes, trees and deposition-induced aliasing of particle noise.
engineering_relevance: It replaces only the field solve, enabling a plug-and-play solver compatible with existing particle methods and time integrators, with O(N_p) complexity for a fixed architecture.
method: Apply a neural operator to the empirical particle measure and evaluate fields at particle positions.
Prove discrete–continuous representation equivalence for any particle count.
Separate sampling, learning and time-stepping errors, and analyze particle noise as implicit regularization.
evidence_signal: Two- and three-dimensional electrostatic benchmarks include Landau damping, plasma instabilities, a cyclotron mini-app and a Penning trap; one model trained across multiple mini-apps remained stable up to twice the training time window.
watch_item: Training particle counts affect noise regularization and should be chosen with inference particle counts in mind; broader long-time generalization remains to be established.
paper_title: NEOPIC: A Neural Operator Framework for Particle-based Kinetic Plasma Simulations
